Rashi on Shabbat 130a:11:1.hebrew: נאמר לא תאכלו כל נבלה ונאמר - באותו פסוק עצמו "לא תבשל גדי", משמע כל האסור משום נבלה נוהג בו איסור בשר בחלב:
Rashi on Shabbat 130a:11:1.english: It is stated, "You shall not eat anything that dies of itself," and it is stated - In that very same verse, "You shall not cook a kid" [is stated], implying [that] anything prohibited due to neveilah is subject to the prohibition of meat in milk.

Rashi on Shabbat 130a:13:1.hebrew: שש אנכי על אמרתך - אמירה יחידה שקדמה לשאר אמירות, והיא מילה שישראל עושין וששים עליה, דכל שאר מצות אינן מוכיחות כל שעה — כגון תפילין ומזוזה וציצית, דאינן כשהוא בשדה וערום בבית המרחץ — אבל זו מעיד עליהם לעולם, כדאמרינן במנחות (דף מג:) בדוד שראה עצמו בבית המרחץ ונצטער. אמר: "אוי לי שאני ערום מכל מצות!" כיון שנסתכל במילה, נתיישבה דעתו:
Rashi on Shabbat 130a:13:1.english: I rejoice at Your word - A singular utterance that preceded the other utterances, and it is circumcision, which Israel performs and rejoices over; for all other mitzvot do not attest [to them] at all times — such as tefillin, mezuzah, and tzitzit, which are not [present] when one is in the field or naked in the bathhouse — whereas this [circumcision] testifies regarding them always, as we say in Menachot (43b) regarding David, who saw himself in the bathhouse and became distressed. He said: "Woe is to me, that I am naked of all mitzvot!" Once he looked at [his] circumcision, his mind was put at ease.

Rashi on Shabbat 130a:13:2.english: With joy - For they make a feast.

Rashi on Shabbat 130a:13:3.english: Over matters of their families - For female relatives were forbidden to them.

Rashi on Shabbat 130a:15:1.hebrew: דא"ר ינאי תפילין צריכות גוף נקי - שלא יפיח. אלמא לא זהירי בהו, ושמעינן מינה דלא מסרו עליה אלא אלישע לבדו:
Rashi on Shabbat 130a:15:1.english: As Rabbi Yannai said: Phylacteries require a clean body - [Meaning] that one should not pass wind [in them]. Evidently, they were not careful with them, and we learn from this that none sacrificed [their lives] for it except Elisha alone.

Rashi on Shabbat 130a:16:1.hebrew: יקרו - פוריי"ר בלעז, לשון ״יקרוה עורבי נחל״ (משלי ל), ולשון ״תנקר לא נעלה״ (במדבר טז):
Rashi on Shabbat 130a:16:1.english: They would pierce [yikru] - Forer in Old French [meaning "to pierce/bore"], [related to] the expression "the ravens of the valley shall pick it out [yikruha]" (Proverbs 30), and the expression "[even if you] gouge out [tenakker]... we will not go up" (Numbers 16).

Rashi on Shabbat 130a:16:2.english: His brain - [The part] that is opposite the tefillin.

Rashi on Shabbat 130a:17:1.english: Protect them - [A dove] does not fight with its beak, but rather with its wings.

Rashi on Shabbat 130a:1:1.hebrew: רבי אליעזר אומר אם לא הביא כלי - איזמל למול את התינוק. וקאי אמתניתין דפרקין דלעיל דסליק מיניה, "וכל צרכי מילה עושין בשבת":
Rashi on Shabbat 130a:1:1.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: If he did not bring an implement - A scalpel to circumcise the infant. And [this] refers to the Mishnah of the previous chapter, with which [it] concluded: "And all necessities of circumcision are performed on Shabbat."

Rashi on Shabbat 130a:1:2.hebrew: מגולה - בפני הכל, ובגמרא מפרש אמאי מצריך ליה לגלוייה:
Rashi on Shabbat 130a:1:2.english: Uncovered - In front of everyone, and in the Gemara it explains why [the Tanna] requires him to uncover it.

Rashi on Shabbat 130a:1:3.english: And in [times of] danger - When the gentiles decreed against circumcision.

Rashi on Shabbat 130a:1:4.hebrew: מכסהו ע"פ עדים - שיעידו שאיזמל של מצוה הוא מביא, ולא יחשדוהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 130a:1:4.english: He covers it in the presence of witnesses - So that they will testify that it is a scalpel for a mitzvah that he is bringing, and they will not suspect him.

Rashi on Shabbat 130a:3:1.hebrew: כלל אמר ר"ע - נחלק על ר"א במכשירי מצוה, שאין דוחין הואיל ואפשר לעשותן מע"ש:
Rashi on Shabbat 130a:3:1.english: Rabbi Akiva stated a principle - He disagrees with Rabbi Eliezer regarding the preliminaries of a mitzvah, [holding] that they do not override [Shabbat], since it is possible to perform them on Shabbat eve.

Rashi on Shabbat 130a:3:2.hebrew: [ושאי אפשר לעשות מע"ש - כגון] מילה עצמה שא"א לה ליעשות, דזמנה ביום השמיני, דוחה שבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 130a:3:2.english: [And that which cannot be done on Shabbat eve - for example,] circumcision itself, which cannot be done [then], since its [appointed] time is on the eighth day, overrides Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 130a:4:1.hebrew: טעמא דר"א - דאמר: מגולה אין, מכוסה לא:
Rashi on Shabbat 130a:4:1.english: The reason of Rabbi Eliezer - Who said: uncovered, yes; covered, no.

Rashi on Shabbat 130a:4:2.english: Due to affection for the mitzvah - To make known that the mitzvah is dear to him, [in] that he desecrates Shabbat for it.

Rashi on Shabbat 130a:4:3.hebrew: משום חשדא - שלא יחשדוהו שהוא נושא שאר חפציו. וסיפא דמתני', דקתני ובסכנה מכסהו ע"פ עדים, ודאי משום חשדא הוא; אלא רישא מיבעיא לן: דוקא מגולה קאמר, אבל מכוסה ע"פ עדים שלא בשעת הסכנה לא, ומשום חיבוב מצוה, או לאו דוקא מגולה, דטעמיה משום חשדא, וה"ה למכוסה על פי עדים:
Rashi on Shabbat 130a:4:3.english: Due to suspicion - So that [people] will not suspect him of carrying his other belongings. And the latter clause of the Mishnah, which teaches, "and in [a time of] danger he covers it in the presence of witnesses," is certainly due to suspicion; rather, we have a dilemma regarding the first clause: [did he] specifically mean uncovered — whereas covered in the presence of witnesses when not in a time of danger, no — and [thus his reason is] due to affection for the mitzvah; or [did he] not specifically [mean] uncovered, because his reason is due to suspicion, and the same applies to [bringing it] covered in the presence of witnesses.

Rashi on Shabbat 130a:8:1.hebrew: אי אמרת בשלמא הוא ותרי שפיר - היינו דמיקרו עדים; אלא הוא וחד מי מיקרי עדים? איהו לגביה נפשיה מי מיקרי עד?:
Rashi on Shabbat 130a:8:1.english: Granted, if you say [it means] him and two [others], [it is] well - That is why they are called "witnesses." But [if it means] him and one [other], are they called "witnesses"? Is he, with respect to himself, called a witness?

Rashi on Shabbat 130a:8:2.hebrew: ומשני שראוים להעיד במקום אחר - לעולם הכא עדות לא שייכא, דלאפוקי מחשדא בעלמא הוא, ואין כאן לא דיני ממונות ולא דיני נפשות שיהו שנים. ומאי קרו להו עדים? דאיכא גילוי מילתא ע"י השני, ושנים קרו עדים בעדות אחריתי שאינו נוגע בה:
Rashi on Shabbat 130a:8:2.english: And [the Gemara] answers: [Because] they are fit to testify elsewhere - Actually, testimony is not relevant here, for it is merely to remove suspicion, and there are neither monetary cases nor capital cases here that two [witnesses] should be required. And why does [the Mishnah] call them "witnesses"? Because there is disclosure of the matter through the second [person], and the two [of them] are called "witnesses" with respect to another testimony in which he has no personal interest.

Rashi on Shabbat 130a:9:1.english: To fashion iron - For a circumcision knife.

Rashi on Shabbat 130a:9:2.english: They would eat poultry meat in milk - as [stated] below.

Tosafot on Shabbat 130a:13:1.hebrew: שש אנכי - במדרש (שוחר טוב): "למנצח על השמינית" כתיב, הנדרש על המילה שהיא בשמיני. וכן אמרי' (פר"א פ' כ"ט): "ויעש אברהם משתה גדול ביום הגמל את יצחק" — ביום ה"ג מל את יצחק, דהיינו ביום השמיני דמילה, כמנין ה"ג. ר"ת:
Tosafot on Shabbat 130a:13:1.english: "I rejoice" - In Midrash (Shocher Tov), "For the leader, on the sheminit" is written, which is expounded regarding circumcision, which is on the eighth [day]. And similarly they say (Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer, ch. 29): "And Abraham made a great feast on the day that Isaac was weaned [higamel]" — on the day of hei-gimel, he circumcised [mal] Isaac, that is, on the eighth day of circumcision, according to the numerical value of hei-gimel [five plus three, totaling eight]. Rabbeinu Tam.

Tosafot on Shabbat 130a:16:1.english: He said to him, "A dove's wings" - Behold, he did not give himself over [to death] to say, "They are phylacteries." Rabbeinu Shmuel.

Tosafot on Shabbat 130a:1:1.hebrew: רבי אליעזר אומר אם לא הביא כלי כו' מביאו בשבת מגולה - וא"ת: ויביאו התינוק אצל כלי, דהשתא ליכא איסור שבת כלל, דהחי נושא את עצמו? וי"ל: דקטן צריך לאמו הוא, ואחר המילה היה צריך להחזירו לאמו, ואז הוי כפות לפי שהוא חולה, כדאמרינן ביומא (דף סו:): "אפי' תימא ר' נתן — חולה שאני". וגם אמו שהיא מסוכנת לא תוכל לבא אצל התינוק. ועוד י"ל: כיון דיותר בקל יביא הכלי משיביא התינוק, שרי ר"א כדי למהר המצוה, כדמוכח בגמרא דאמר: פעם אחת שכחו ולא הביאו איזמל מע"ש, והביאו בשבת שלא ברצונו, שהביאו דרך חצרות וגגות וקרפיפות, והיו יכולין להביא דרך רה"ר — אלמא דשרי ר"א דרך רה"ר, דהוי דאורייתא, כדי למהר המצוה, אע"פ שיכול לעשות [בענין] דליכא אלא איסורא דרבנן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 130a:1:1.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: If he did not bring an implement, etc., he brings it on Shabbat uncovered - And if you ask: Let them bring the infant to the implement, for then there is no Shabbat prohibition at all, since a living creature carries itself? And one can answer: A young child needs his mother, and after the circumcision it would be necessary to return him to his mother, and then he is [like] one who is bound because he is ill, as we say in Yoma (66b): "Even if you say [it follows] Rabbi Natan, an ill person is different." And furthermore, his mother, who is in danger [from childbirth], cannot come to the infant. And furthermore, one can answer: Since one can bring the implement more easily than one can bring the infant, Rabbi Eliezer permits [it] in order to hasten the mitzvah, as is proven in the Gemara, which says: Once they forgot and did not bring a scalpel on Shabbat eve, and they brought it on Shabbat against his will, for they brought it via courtyards, roofs, and enclosures, whereas they could have brought [it] via the public domain. Thus, Rabbi Eliezer permits [bringing it] via the public domain, which is a Torah [prohibition], in order to hasten the mitzvah, even though one can do [it in a manner] where there is only a rabbinic prohibition.
